why: The statement asks for the full GUE pair correlation of zeta zeros. The Claude-credited work (Anthropic post, Alpöge–Furman, Lamzouri) moves the proportion of simple and critical-line zeros, a different quantity, so I scored it variant even though the AI role is real (generated for the first two; Lamzouri is assisted because he adds his own estimates to Claude's argument). The Goldston et al. papers take the conjecture as a hypothesis or change it, so they are none or variant. Jerby's paper claims the full law but only under RH. The bullet does not state RH, so I read the result as a conditional restriction (case), not whole. I marked it doubtful rather than not_credible: the author has relevant prior work on the Z-function, but the steps I could see are heuristic and nobody has engaged with it. Tishkov's unconditional claim matches the scope, but several F10 signals line up: an independent author with parallel RH-proof claims, a venue that reviews nothing, self-citation to unreviewed work, no uptake on a landmark problem, and the reference article still calls the conjecture open. So it is not_credible. Baluyot 2023 (the restricted-range theorem, refereed) is a pre-snapshot case. The tishkov ergodic event is dated 2026 by year only, which still places it after the snapshot.
doubts: Whether an RH-conditional proof answers the bullet is a close call. The classical formulation assumes RH, so Jerby could arguably be whole; I chose case because the bullet's own wording is unconditional. Jerby's proof section was never read. The Lamzouri assisted-versus-generated split rests on the abstract alone.
